tagline: A mile and a half of lumber money, set back.
intro: Center Avenue runs east out of downtown Bay City for a mile and a half, from Madison Avenue to Livingston Street, and most of the way it is a tree-lined street of big Victorian houses set back on broad lawns. M-25 follows it the whole length, and M-15 comes up Trumbull Street to end at it.

Bay City built its first sawmill in 1837 and had a dozen by 1854. The families who made their money in lumber and salt began building here in the 1870s, close to the business district but quiet. When lumbering declined after the turn of the century, the next round of money built in among them, and farther east.

moments.title: James Shearer Residence, 701 Center Avenue
moments.text: A grand Italianate house of 1876 at the older, western end of the avenue, where the building started.

moments.title: Frederick Bradley Residence, 1400 Center Avenue
moments.text: A massive Queen Anne house finished in 1889, built to a complexly asymmetrical plan and given two elaborate porches.

moments.title: Henry Clements Residence, 1601 Center Avenue
moments.text: Built in 1890, a house in the French chateau manner, under a steeply hipped roof.
